# Remesso SDK documentation

> Recurring and agent payments on Celo, in TypeScript.

Every page of https://docs.remesso.xyz for remesso-sdk 0.3.1, in the order of its sidebar. Each page starts with a level-1 heading and its URL.

# Introduction

> What remesso-sdk is, what you can build with it, and how a payment moves from a signature to a webhook.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs

`remesso-sdk` is a TypeScript library for payments in stablecoins on Celo, between people and between agents. A payer signs once and Remesso's executor sends each payment when it is due; an agent pays from its own wallet or within a policy a person set; and the recipient checks every payment on the chain and hears about it from a signed webhook.

To build one agent that sells and another that pays it, start with [Build an agent-to-agent app](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-to-agent). For several workers, signed invoices and recovery after a crash, see [Run an agent service in production](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/production-sdk).

```bash
npm install remesso-sdk viem
```

## What you can build

- **Payments on a schedule.** A payer authorises a fixed amount to a fixed address on a fixed cadence: a monthly retainer, a weekly allowance, payroll, a remittance home. Remesso sends each payment when it is due. Nobody can change the recipient, the amount or the cadence afterwards; cancelling is the only edit.
- **Payments by an agent, within limits.** A person grants their AI agent's key a policy: one token, a cap per payment and per day, an expiry, optionally a list of the only recipients allowed. The agent pays from the person's wallet, and the contract refuses anything outside the policy. A payment retried with the same idempotency key pays once.
- **Getting paid.** Ask a wallet to pay you with a payment request, share a link that opens the payer's form filled in, and see when the payment arrives.
- **Knowing you were paid.** Payment events and signed webhooks tell you about every payment to an address, without running a node or an indexer.
- **Credit for the volume you bring.** Your own ERC-8021 builder code rides on every payment of the schedules your app creates.

## How a payment moves

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant P as Payer's wallet
    participant C as Remesso contract
    participant E as Remesso executor
    participant R as Recipient
    participant W as Your webhook
    P->>C: approve and createSchedule (signed once)
    loop each time a payment is due
        E->>C: executeRun(schedule)
        C->>R: the amount, less the 0.25% fee
        E-->>W: payment.received (signed)
    end
    Note over W: payment.finalized follows once Celo finalizes the block
```

The payer's signature is the authority. The contract checks every payment against what was signed: the recipient, the amount, the cadence, the number of payments and the expiry. Remesso's executor can only ask the contract to send a payment that is due; it cannot redirect one, enlarge one or send one early unless the payer allowed it.

## The building blocks

| | What it is | Who signs | Who pays gas |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Schedules](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules) | A payer's standing instruction, held by the `RemessoExecutorV5` contract | The payer, once | The payer to create it, Remesso's executor for each payment |
| [Agent payments](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments) | Spending limits a person grants an agent, held by `RemessoAgentAllowance` | The person for the policy, the agent for each payment | The agent |
| [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests) | "Please pay me", with states, stored by Remesso's backend | Nobody: a request moves no money | Nobody |
| [Payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events) and [webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks) | Every payment to or from an address, read from the chain by Remesso's indexer | Nobody | Nobody |

## Before you start

- You need Node 20 or later, and a little USDT on Celo for your first payment.
- The SDK runs on a server or in a script with a private key. In a browser it works with the user's own wallet.
- Wallet-funded sends and schedules follow the executor's per-run limits. Policy payments follow their signed spending caps. See [fees, limits and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas).

## Where to go next

- **[Quickstart](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/quickstart):** send a payment and receive its webhook in about 15 minutes.
- **[Core concepts](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/concepts):** schedules, the executor, policies, requests, events and finality.
- **[Use cases](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases):** subscriptions, payroll, remittances, an allowance and an AI agent's budget, built end to end.
- **[API reference](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/client):** every option, method and return value.
- **[Build with AI](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/build-with-ai):** these docs as a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, or as one text file for any chat.

# Quickstart

> Send a 1 USDT payment on a schedule and receive its signed webhook, from an empty folder, in about 15 minutes.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/quickstart

This walkthrough takes you from an empty folder to a real payment and the signed webhook that reports it. It takes about 15 minutes, most of it waiting for the payment to be picked up.

You will run two programs: a **receiver**, which serves a webhook endpoint, and a **payer**, which creates a schedule that pays the receiver 1 USDT once.

## What you need

- Node 20 or later.
- About **1.05 USDT on Celo** in a wallet you control, for the payment and the fee. A little CELO for gas helps; without it, the SDK pays gas in USDT.
- `cloudflared`, to give your laptop a public HTTPS address for the webhook ([install it](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/downloads/)). Any public HTTPS URL works instead.

## 1. Create the project

The SDK is ES modules only, and `tsx` runs TypeScript files without a build step.

```bash
mkdir remesso-quickstart && cd remesso-quickstart
npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install remesso-sdk viem
npm install -D tsx
```

## 2. Make two keys

One key pays and the other receives. Save this as `keys.ts` and run `npx tsx keys.ts` twice:

```ts title="keys.ts"
import { generatePrivateKey, privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const key = generatePrivateKey();
console.log(key, privateKeyToAccount(key).address);
```

Send about 1.05 USDT to the payer's address on Celo. The receiver needs nothing: receiving costs no gas. Then export the keys in each terminal you use:

```bash
export PAYER_KEY=0x… RECEIVER_KEY=0x… RECEIVER=0x…
```

## 3. Run the receiver

In a first terminal, open a public address that forwards to port 8787. A Cloudflare quick tunnel needs no account and prints a `trycloudflare.com` URL:

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8787
```

In a second terminal, save this as `receiver.ts`. It serves the webhook endpoint and prints each payment it is told about:

```ts title="receiver.ts"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createRemesso, formatAmount, webhookHandler } from "remesso-sdk";
import { toNodeListener } from "remesso-sdk/node";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const receiver = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.RECEIVER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

// Remesso returns the signing secret once your endpoint has answered its
// challenge, so the handler reads it when each delivery arrives.
let secret: string | undefined;

const handler = webhookHandler({
  recipient: receiver.address,
  secret: () => secret,
  onPayment: (m) =>
    console.log(m.type, formatAmount(m.data.amount, m.data.token), m.data.final ? "final" : "not final yet", m.data.txHash),
});

const server = createServer(toNodeListener(handler));
await new Promise<void>((done) => server.listen(8787, done));

const sub = await receiver.webhooks.subscribe({ url: process.env.PUBLIC_URL! });
secret = sub.secret; // returned once: store it if the receiver must survive a restart
console.log("subscribed", sub.subscription, "for", receiver.address);
```

Run it with the tunnel's URL:

```bash
PUBLIC_URL=https://….trycloudflare.com npx tsx receiver.ts
```

When you subscribe, Remesso first posts a challenge to your URL. The handler answers it only for the address you configured, and Remesso then returns the signing secret, once. You should see `subscribed`.

> **Tip**
>
> A quick tunnel gets a new URL every time it starts, and an address can hold five subscriptions. Remove old ones with `receiver.webhooks.revoke({ url })`.

## 4. Pay

In a third terminal, save this as `pay.ts` and run `npx tsx pay.ts`. It sends two transactions: an approval for the contract, then the schedule itself, one payment of 1 USDT.

```ts title="pay.ts"
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const payer = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PAYER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

const s = await payer.schedules.create({
  to: process.env.RECEIVER!,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  every: "week",
  runs: 1,
});
console.log("schedule", s.id, "pays", formatAmount(s.recipientGets, "USDT"), s.hash);
```

The output shows the schedule's id and what the recipient gets: `0.9975 USDT`, which is 1 USDT less the 0.25% fee.

## 5. Watch the payment arrive

Go back to the receiver's terminal and wait.

1. Remesso finds a schedule created outside its own app within about **5 minutes**, and sends the payment within a minute of that.
2. A minute or two later the handler prints `payment.received` with `not final yet`: 0.9975 USDT.
3. About **25 to 30 minutes** later, `payment.finalized` follows, once Celo has finalized the block.

A delivery that fails is retried with the same `webhook-id` for 24 hours, so a real handler deduplicates on it.

## No public URL? Poll instead

The same information is available without a webhook. Payment events come from Remesso's indexer, and `watch` yields each new one:

```ts title="watch.ts"
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const receiver = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.RECEIVER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

for await (const e of receiver.events.watch({ role: "to", kinds: ["run", "policy_payment"] })) {
  console.log(e.kind, formatAmount(e.amount!, e.token!), e.final ? "final" : "not final yet", e.txHash);
}
```

## What just happened

- The payer **signed a mandate**: one payment of 1 USDT to the receiver. The contract holds it, and nothing can change its recipient or amount.
- Remesso's **executor** sent the payment when it was due. It paid the gas; the payer paid only for the approval and the schedule.
- Remesso's **indexer** read the payment from the chain and delivered a **signed webhook**, then a second one when the block became final.

## Next steps

- [Core concepts](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/concepts) explains schedules, the executor and finality in more depth.
- [Pay on a schedule](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules) covers cadences, triggers, pausing and cancelling.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks) shows how to run the handler in Express, Next.js, Deno or Cloudflare Workers.
- [Use cases](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases) builds complete products on these pieces.

# Installation and setup

> Install remesso-sdk, create a client for a server, a browser wallet or read-only use, and keep its keys safe.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation

This page covers installing the SDK, the three ways to create a client, and how to handle the keys it signs with.

## Requirements

- **Node 20 or later.** The SDK also runs in Deno through `npm:` specifiers.
- **ES modules.** The package is ESM. In a Node project, set `"type": "module"` in `package.json` or use `.mjs` and `.mts` files. Node 20.19 and 22.12 or later can also `require()` it from CommonJS.
- **viem 2.21 or later** as a peer dependency. The SDK signs and reads through viem, and accepts viem accounts and clients.
- **Celo mainnet.** The SDK refuses to sign on any other chain. There is no testnet.

## Install

**npm**

```bash
npm install remesso-sdk viem
```

**pnpm**

```bash
pnpm add remesso-sdk viem
```

**yarn**

```bash
yarn add remesso-sdk viem
```

**Deno**

```ts
import { createRemesso } from "npm:remesso-sdk";
```

The package has two entry points:

| Import | For |
|---|---|
| `remesso-sdk` | Everything that runs anywhere: the client, webhook verification, token and fee helpers. |
| `remesso-sdk/node` | Node only: `fileStore` (agent payment records on disk), `safeFetchText` and `toNodeListener`. |

## Create a client

Every feature hangs off one client, created with `createRemesso`. What you pass decides what it can do.

### With a private key

On a server, in a script or in an agent, give it a viem account. The client can then pay, create schedules, sign requests and subscribe to webhooks.

```ts title="client.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const remesso = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.REMESSO_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

console.log(remesso.address); // the account's address
```

### With a browser wallet

In a web app, pass the user's own wallet as a viem wallet client on Celo. The user approves each transaction in their wallet. Agent payments are the exception: they are signed before they are sent, so they need a local account like the one above.

```ts title="browser.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { createWalletClient, custom, type EIP1193Provider } from "viem";
import { celo } from "viem/chains";

declare const ethereum: EIP1193Provider; // window.ethereum, injected by the wallet

const [address] = await ethereum.request({ method: "eth_requestAccounts" });
const wallet = createWalletClient({ account: address, chain: celo, transport: custom(ethereum) });

const remesso = createRemesso({ walletClient: wallet });
```

### Read-only

Without an account, the client reads: schedules, policies, requests, payment events and agents. Methods that need a signer throw a `no_account` error, and methods that default to "this account" need an address.

```ts title="reader.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";

const reader = createRemesso();

const schedule = await reader.schedules.get(4);
const { events } = await reader.events.list({ address: schedule.to, role: "to" });
console.log(schedule.runsExecuted, "of", schedule.maxRuns, "payments sent;", events.length, "events");
```

## Options

The options you will use most:

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account` | none | A viem account that signs. |
| `walletClient` | none | A viem wallet client instead of an account. |
| `rpcUrl` | `https://forno.celo.org` | A Celo mainnet RPC. The SDK checks it answers chain 42220 before signing anything. |
| `store` | memory | Where agent payments are recorded so a retry pays once. Use `fileStore()` in production. |
| `builderCodes` | none | Your own ERC-8021 codes. See [builder codes](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/builder-codes). |

Every option is in the [client reference](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/client#createremessooptions).

## Keys and safety

The SDK signs with whatever key you give it, and Remesso has no way to reverse a payment.

- **Keep keys out of code.** Read them from the environment or a secrets manager, and never commit them.
- **One key per role.** The wallet that pays on a schedule, the agent's key and the receiving address do different jobs. Keeping them apart limits what one leaked key can do.
- **Hold only what you need.** A schedule spends through an ERC-20 approval, and an agent spends within its policy. Both are limits you set: keep them close to what you intend to pay.
- **The receiving key is optional.** Receiving needs only an address. You need its key only to subscribe to webhooks, answer or decline requests, or sign as that address.

## Check your setup

This reads the chain and Remesso's backend without signing anything:

```ts title="check.ts"
import { CHAIN_ID, createRemesso, EXECUTOR, FEE_BPS } from "remesso-sdk";

const reader = createRemesso();
console.log("chain", CHAIN_ID, "executor", EXECUTOR, "fee", FEE_BPS / 100, "%");
console.log("rpc answers chain", await reader.publicClient.getChainId());
```

## Next steps

- [Core concepts](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/concepts): how schedules, the executor and finality fit together.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/quickstart): a first payment and its webhook.

# Build with AI

> Give Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any AI assistant the whole Remesso documentation, as a skill or as one text file.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/build-with-ai

Every page of this documentation is also published for AI assistants. Install the Remesso skills and your coding assistant reads the right page before it writes Remesso code, or give any chat the whole documentation as one text file.

## What's available

| | What it is | Use it with |
|---|---|---|
| The `remesso-sdk` skill | Every page of this documentation, and the rules for writing code with the SDK | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other assistants that load skills |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/llms-full.txt) | The whole documentation in one text file | Any chat: attach the file or give it the URL |
| [`llms.txt`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/llms.txt) | An index of the pages, each linked as Markdown | Tools that read [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) |
| Each page as Markdown | The page's URL with `.md` added, such as [`/docs/build-with-ai.md`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/build-with-ai.md) | Putting one page into a prompt |

All of them are generated from these pages each time the documentation changes, so they describe the same version of the SDK.

## Install the skills

### Claude Code

Add Remesso's plugin. It carries the skills and the Remesso wallet:

```text
/plugin marketplace add https://bitbucket.org/crackedstudios/remesso.git
/plugin install remesso@remesso
```

To add only the skills, copy them into Claude Code's skills folder:

```bash
npx -y remesso-wallet skills ~/.claude/skills
```

### Codex, Cursor and others

```bash
npx -y remesso-wallet skills
```

This copies the skills to `~/.agents/skills`, where Codex and Cursor look. Give it a folder to put them somewhere else, such as a project's own skills folder. Restart the assistant to load them, and run the command again to update them.

### Any chat

Give the assistant `https://docs.remesso.xyz/llms-full.txt`, or attach the file. It holds every page, with the links between pages as full URLs.

## The skills

| Skill | For |
|---|---|
| `remesso-sdk` | Writing and reviewing code that uses `remesso-sdk` |
| `remesso` | An agent that pays and gets paid through Remesso's endpoints and contracts directly, without the SDK |
| `remesso-x402` | Paying Remesso's paid HTTP services over x402 |
| `remesso-wallet` | The tools of the Remesso wallet, described below |

An assistant loads a skill when your request matches it, so you don't need to name one.

## Prompts to try

- "Using remesso-sdk, ask 0x… to pay 5 USDT every week for four weeks, and print the link to send them."
- "Add a route to my Express server that receives Remesso webhooks and marks an order paid only after verifying the payment on the chain."
- "My agent sells translations. When another agent pays my invoice from its own wallet, deliver the order exactly once, and make retries safe."
- "Start a local fork with `npx remesso-sdk dev` and run my payment code against it."

## Let the assistant pay, too

The skills help an assistant write code. The Remesso wallet lets an assistant make payments itself: it is an MCP server with tools such as `pay`, `request_payment` and `pay_x402`, and it spends only within a [spending policy](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments) you sign on-chain, with a cap per payment and per day and an expiry. You set the policy at [remesso.xyz/agent-wallet](https://remesso.xyz/agent-wallet).

It comes with the Claude Code plugin above. In other MCP hosts, add it as a server that runs:

```bash
npx -y remesso-wallet
```

# Core concepts

> Schedules, the executor, triggers, fees, agent policies, payment requests, payment events, finality and webhooks, and how they fit together.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/concepts

Remesso has a small number of moving parts. This page explains each one and what it guarantees, so the guides that follow read as variations on the same model.

## Celo mainnet, stablecoins only

Remesso runs on Celo mainnet (chain id `42220`) and nowhere else.

Payments are in stablecoins and local-currency tokens: USDT, USDC, USDm and USA₮ (US dollars), Ripio's wARS, wBRL, wCOP, wMXN, wCLP and wPEN (Argentine, Colombian, Mexican and Chilean pesos, Brazilian reais and Peruvian soles), and cNGN (Nigerian naira). Tokens have different decimals: USDT has 6 and wARS has 18. The SDK takes amounts as decimal strings, like `"2.50"`, and returns base units as `bigint`. The full list is in [tokens and limits](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/tokens-and-limits).

## Schedules: a payer signs once

A **schedule** is a standing instruction a payer signs on-chain: this amount, to this address, this often, this many times. It lives in the `RemessoExecutorV5` contract, created with two transactions from the payer's wallet: an ERC-20 approval for the contract, then the schedule itself.

What the payer signs is final:

- **The recipient, the amount and the cadence never change.** Not by Remesso, not by the contract's owner, not by the payer. Cancelling is the only edit.
- **It ends.** A schedule has a number of payments and an expiry, at most a year after it starts.
- **It can be paused and resumed** by the payer, and **cancelled** for good.
- **It spends through the approval.** Revoking the approval stops every future payment, so the payer always keeps a way out.

A payment is gone once it is sent. Remesso can't reverse it, and neither can the payer.

## The executor sends each payment

Remesso's **executor** is a backend service with a key of its own. Every minute it finds schedules that are due and asks the contract to run them. The contract checks each request against what the payer signed. The executor pays the gas for each payment; the payer pays none after creating the schedule.

A few rules shape when a payment goes out:

- **The first payment follows creation within minutes.** A schedule created in the Remesso app is known at once. One created anywhere else, such as with the SDK, is discovered by a sync that runs every five minutes.
- **Each payment must be worth between 1 and 1,000 dollars**, or the same in local currency. A schedule outside those bounds is valid on-chain but the executor never runs it, so the SDK refuses one before you sign. See [fees, limits and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas).
- **A payment that can't go out waits.** If the payer's balance or approval is short when a payment is due, the executor skips it, and it goes out once the payer tops up. Payments aren't caught up in a burst.

## Triggers: bringing a payment forward

A payer can grant a **trigger**: an address allowed to bring the next payment forward. The payment is the same one, with the same recipient and amount. A trigger moves a payment earlier and never adds one. Granting `"remesso"` lets Remesso's executor do it, which is what makes `trigger-run` (a paid early send) usable for that schedule.

## Fees

Remesso takes **0.25% of each scheduled payment**, out of the payment and rounded up. When a payer sends 1 USDT, the recipient receives 0.9975. The fee is pinned in each schedule when it is signed. Agent payments carry no fee, and receiving costs nothing.

When you want the recipient to get an exact amount, ask for it with `receive` and the SDK works out what to send. Payment requests work the same way: a requested amount is what the recipient receives.

## Agent policies: spending within limits

A **policy** lets a person's agent pay from the person's wallet, within limits the person sets. It lives in the `RemessoAgentAllowance` contract, which has no owner and no admin. A policy has:

- one token;
- a cap per payment, and a cap per day: a 24-hour window that opens with the first payment after the previous window has closed;
- an expiry;
- optionally, a list of the only addresses the agent may pay;
- a budget: the person's token approval for the allowance contract, shared by their policies for that token.

The agent's key calls `pay` and pays its own gas. The contract refuses any payment outside the policy, and the person can revoke the policy at any time.

**Idempotency** keeps retries safe. Give each payment you intend an idempotency key, such as an invoice id. A retry with the same key reports the first attempt's outcome and never pays twice, even if the first attempt timed out after it was sent. Without a key, an identical payment within ten minutes is refused.

## Payment requests: asking to be paid

A **payment request** asks a wallet to pay you: how much, in which token, how often. It costs nothing to send. It appears in the payer's Remesso inbox and comes with a link that opens their payment form filled in. A request can't move money: the payer still signs in their own wallet.

A request has a state:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Waiting for the payer. Requests stay live for 30 days. |
| `accepted` | A schedule or payment answered it on the requested terms. |
| `accepted_with_changes` | It was answered, but some terms differ from what was asked. |
| `declined` | The payer, or their agent, turned it down with a signature. |
| `expired` | Not answered in time. |

**Accepted is not paid.** A request counts as paid only when a payment with a transaction is recorded against it.

## Payment events and finality

Remesso's **indexer** reads the contracts every minute and records each payment as a **payment event**: payments sent on a schedule, schedules created, agent payments, and policies created or revoked. You can list them by address, or have them delivered as webhooks.

Two fields matter most:

- **`final`** turns true once the block is at or below Celo's finalized block, about 25 to 30 minutes after the payment. Before that, a payment is very likely to stand but not yet certain. Ship goods or grant access on `final` when the amount warrants it.
- **`removed`** turns true if a chain reorganisation undid the block. The event is kept and marked, never deleted.

Every change to an event gives it a new `seq`, so reading from your last `seq` misses nothing.

## Webhooks

A **webhook** subscription sends an address's payment events to your HTTPS endpoint as they happen. Deliveries follow the Standard Webhooks format and are signed with a secret only you and Remesso know. There are three types: `payment.received`, `payment.finalized` and `payment.removed`.

Delivery is at least once: a failed delivery is retried with the same `webhook-id` for 24 hours. Deduplicate on that id.

## Builder codes

Celo credits on-chain activity to the app that caused it, through ERC-8021 attribution codes on each transaction. Every transaction the SDK sends carries Remesso's codes. Add your own **builder code** and it rides along too, including on every payment Remesso sends for the schedules your app creates. See [builder codes](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/builder-codes).

## Reads can lag behind writes

Celo's public RPC is several nodes behind a load balancer. For a few seconds after a transaction lands, a read can come from a node that hasn't seen it. The SDK waits for things it has just created to become visible, and retries an answer to a request while the backend can't see the schedule yet. In your own code, expect a balance or a status read straight after a transaction to be a block behind, and read again.

## What is on-chain and what isn't

| On-chain, enforced by contracts | Off-chain, run by Remesso |
|---|---|
| Schedules and everything they pin | The executor that sends due payments |
| Agent policies and their limits | Payment requests and their states |
| Every payment, and its recipient and amount | The indexer, payment events and webhooks |

The contracts are the authority. If Remesso's backend stopped, no schedule could pay more, pay someone else or pay earlier than its payer allowed; scheduled payments would simply wait until it came back. Agent payments go straight to the contract, so they keep working.

## Next steps

- [Pay on a schedule](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules)
- [Agent payments](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments)
- [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests)

---

# Build an agent-to-agent app

> One agent asks another to pay, gets paid from a wallet or a spending policy, and checks the payment on the chain before it delivers.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-to-agent

One agent sells a service and another buys it. The seller asks to be paid, the buyer pays from its own wallet or from a spending policy a person gave it, and the seller checks the payment on the chain before it delivers. This guide builds both sides.

The APIs on this page need `remesso-sdk` 0.3.0 or later.

## Two ways to fund a payment

| Funding | Whose money moves | Setup | Remesso's fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wallet` | The buying agent's own wallet | The agent holds the token and a little CELO for gas | 0.25%, added to what the buyer pays, so the seller receives the exact amount |
| `policy` | A person's or a treasury's wallet | Its owner creates a [spending policy](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments) that names the agent | None |

In both, `amount` is what the seller receives: `amount: "1"` with `token: "USDT"` delivers exactly 1 USDT.

A wallet payment is a [schedule](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules) with a single payment. The SDK creates it, approves the token and runs it at once: three transactions, about 370,000 gas together. A policy payment is one transaction, about 90,000 gas. Remesso indexes both, so requests, events and webhooks treat them the same way.

## Create the clients

```ts
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { fileRemittanceStore, fileStore, safeFetchText } from "remesso-sdk/node";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

// The buying agent. Its journals record each payment before it is sent, so a
// retry after a crash or a timeout never pays twice.
const buyer = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.BUYER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
  store: fileStore("./state/policy-payments.json"),
  remittanceStore: fileRemittanceStore("./state/wallet-payments.json"),
  fetchText: safeFetchText,
});

// The selling agent.
const seller = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.SELLER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
```

Keep the journal files. Without them the SDK keeps its records in memory, and a retry after a restart could pay a second time. Each file serves one process. For several workers, see [sharing journals across workers](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/production-sdk#share-journals-across-workers).

## 1. The seller asks to be paid

The seller asks the wallet whose money will move: the buyer's own address for wallet funding, or the policy owner's address for policy funding.

```ts
const invoice = await seller.requests.create({
  payer: buyer.address,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  runs: 1,
  from: "Translation agent",
  note: "Translate order 1042",
});
const requestId = invoice.id;
```

A request moves no money, and anyone can create one. When the buyer needs proof that the seller asked, use a [signed invoice](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/production-sdk#sign-an-invoice) instead. Recurring requests are for [schedules](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules); `remittances.send` pays one-off requests only.

## 2. The buyer pays from its own wallet

```ts
const sent = await buyer.remittances.send({
  funding: "wallet",
  to: seller.address,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  requestId,
  idempotencyKey: `request:${requestId}`,
});
console.log(sent.status, sent.stage, sent.hash);
```

The request must name this wallet as the payer and these exact terms. The SDK approves and runs the payment only once Remesso has recorded that this payment answers the request, since that is what the seller checks; if the request was declined or answered by another payment in the meantime, the payment is cancelled instead. A `confirmed` result carries `hash`, the transaction that paid.

A `pending` result may still be paid. Call `send` again with the same key and terms, at any time: the SDK continues the same payment from its journal and never creates a second one. Don't retry a pending payment under a new key; that is a second payment. `stage` says where it stands: `creation`, `approval`, `execution` or `cancellation`.

If the payment can't be completed, for instance because the wallet's balance dropped, the SDK cancels its schedule, so that it can't be paid later either. Only once the cancellation has landed does it report that nothing was paid: a `refused` error whose `details.cancelled` is `true`. Until then the result is `pending`, with a `cancellationHash`.

## 3. Or the buyer pays from a spending policy

The person or treasury creates a policy once, as in [agent payments](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments), and the request names that owner as the payer:

```ts
const sent = await buyer.remittances.send({
  funding: "policy",
  policyId,
  to: seller.address,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  requestId,
  idempotencyKey: `request:${requestId}`,
});
console.log(sent.status, sent.payer); // payer is the policy's owner
```

The payment carries the request's reference in its memo, which is how Remesso knows it answers this request. The contract enforces the policy's caps per payment and per day, its recipient list and its expiry.

## Pay a registered agent

When the seller has an ERC-8004 identity with a Remesso payee profile (see [finding agents](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/find-agents)), `agents.pay` takes the wallet to pay from the registry:

```ts
declare const sellerAgentId: bigint; // the seller's ERC-8004 id
const paid = await buyer.agents.pay(sellerAgentId, {
  funding: "wallet",
  requestId,
  expectedWallet: seller.address,
});
console.log(paid.counterparty, paid.status, paid.hash);
```

The SDK checks the token the profile accepts, the request reference it requires and that the request pays the registered wallet, then reads the registry again just before it sends. With `expectedWallet`, it refuses if the registered wallet isn't the one your application approved. It never takes a wallet from the profile's JSON.

Without a request, pass `amount`, `token` and an `idempotencyKey` instead; the profile must accept payments without a reference. For a policy, set `funding: "policy"` and optionally `policyId`.

## 4. The seller checks the payment before it delivers

Checking a payment needs no key, no webhook and nothing from Remesso's indexer:

```ts
declare const txHash: `0x${string}`;
const proof = await reader.receipts.verify({
  txHash,
  from: buyer.address,
  to: seller.address,
  token: "USDT",
  amount: "1",
  scheduleId,
  finality: "finalized",
});
console.log(proof.eventId, proof.amount, proof.finality);
```

`verify` reads the transaction's receipt and checks that it holds a payment of exactly this token and amount, from this payer to this recipient, made by Remesso's contracts, in a block that is still on the chain. A schedule's amounts are what arrived, after the fee. For a policy payment, pass `policyId` and `memo` instead of `scheduleId`.

With `finality: "finalized"` it also refuses until Celo has finalized the block, about 25 minutes after the payment. `included` answers at once, but a payment that is only included can still be undone by a reorganization.

Before delivering, store `proof.eventId` under a unique constraint, in the same database transaction that marks the order fulfilled, so one payment can never fulfil two orders.

[Payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events) and [webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks) tell you when to check: something arrived. `verify` tells you it is the payment you expect.

## Run the example

The repository's `examples/agent-to-agent.ts` runs both sides from the command line:

```bash
deno run --allow-all --config examples/sdk.deno.json --unstable-sloppy-imports examples/agent-to-agent.ts request
deno run --allow-all --config examples/sdk.deno.json --unstable-sloppy-imports examples/agent-to-agent.ts pay
deno run --allow-all --config examples/sdk.deno.json --unstable-sloppy-imports examples/agent-to-agent.ts verify
```

- `request`, as the seller: set `SELLER_KEY`, `PAYER_ADDRESS` and `AMOUNT`, and optionally `TOKEN`. It prints the `REQUEST_ID`.
- `pay`, as the buyer: set `BUYER_KEY`, `FUNDING` (`wallet` or `policy`), `REQUEST_ID`, `SELLER_ADDRESS` and `AMOUNT`, and optionally `TOKEN` and `SELLER_AGENT_ID`. Policy funding also needs `POLICY_ID`. It shows what it would do; add `--send` to pay. `POLICY_STORE` and `WALLET_STORE` set where the journals live.
- `verify`, as the seller: set `TX_HASH`, `PAYER_ADDRESS`, `SELLER_ADDRESS`, `AMOUNT`, `TOKEN`, and `SCHEDULE_ID` or `POLICY_ID` (with `REQUEST_ID` for the memo). It waits for finality unless you set `FINALITY=included`.

The example pays on Celo mainnet unless `RPC_URL` points at a local fork.

---

# Run an agent service in production

> Workers that share one key, quotes, deadlines, signed invoices, recovery after a crash, local development, managed signers and agent tools.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/production-sdk

The [agent-to-agent guide](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-to-agent) covers one buyer and one seller. This page covers what a service needs around them: several workers sharing a key, quotes and deadlines, signed invoices, recovery after a crash, and local development.

The APIs on this page need `remesso-sdk` 0.3.0 or later.

## Try both funding models locally

With Foundry's `anvil` installed and Node 20 or later:

```bash
npx remesso-sdk dev --smoke
```

This forks Celo mainnet into a local Anvil, funds public test accounts on it, starts an in-memory stand-in for Remesso's backend with a webhook receiver, pays once from a wallet and once from a policy, checks both, and cleans up. Without `--smoke` it keeps running and prints the settings and test keys to use. Every transaction goes to the local fork; Celo mainnet only supplies the state it starts from. Never fund the public test keys on a real network.

The stand-in backend isn't Remesso's: its timing, cron and finality are not production's. The same environment is available to a test suite:

```ts
import { startDev } from "remesso-sdk/dev";

const dev = await startDev();
try {
  console.log(dev.sampleInvoice.id, dev.receiverUrl);
  await dev.smoke();
} finally {
  await dev.close();
}
```

## Share journals across workers

Every process that signs with the same key must use the same journals and the same lock, or two workers could each pay the same order. With PostgreSQL (`postgres@3.4.5`), one call gives all four:

```ts
import postgres from "postgres";
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { createPostgresStorage } from "remesso-sdk/postgres";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const sql = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL!, {
  max: 8,
  connection: { synchronous_commit: "on" },
});
const storage = createPostgresStorage(sql, { namespace: "my-agent-service" });
await storage.initialize(); // Once, before the workers start.

const agent = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.AGENT_KEY as `0x${string}`),
  store: storage.paymentStore,
  remittanceStore: storage.remittanceStore,
  invoiceStore: storage.invoiceStore,
  coordinator: storage.coordinator,
});
```

`createRemesso` refuses a `coordinator` without the three stores: with journals in memory, each worker would keep its own record of keys, and a retry on another worker would pay again.

A session lock is held from reading the journal to broadcasting, so connect directly or through session pooling; transaction pooling can't hold it. If the connection is lost, the SDK stops before signing or sending anything more.

`initialize()` creates the SDK's own tables and turns on row-level security; signed transactions are stored in them, so keep them readable only by the server role that owns them. The package's `POSTGRES.md` has complete examples.

### When a transaction isn't sent

Every transaction is saved before it is broadcast. If a broadcast fails, the SDK retries it at once, and before signing anything new it sends again any saved transaction the network still doesn't have, lowest nonce first. So one lost broadcast can't hold up every transaction after it.

A saved transaction that must no longer land is cancelled instead of sent: the SDK signs a transaction that does nothing at the same nonce, and only one of the two can ever be mined. The no-op pays more than the original, so a node still holding the original takes the no-op instead. This happens to a policy payment still unsent close to its `validUntil`, including one whose deadline passes while it is being saved, and to a contract write (a schedule or a policy) whose caller was told it couldn't be broadcast; one saved in the last 30 seconds is given that long to arrive first.

## Quote and bound a payment

```ts
const prepared = await payer.remittances.prepare({
  funding: "wallet",
  to: receiver.address,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  idempotencyKey: "order-123",
  maxDebit: "1.01", // The most the payer's balance may lose, fee included; gas is separate.
}, { ttlSeconds: 60 });

console.log(prepared.quote.protocolFee, prepared.quote.approval);
console.log(prepared.quote.gas.steps, prepared.quote.gas.notes);
const sent = await payer.remittances.send(prepared.input);
console.log(sent.status, sent.hash);
```

`quote()` signs nothing. It reports whether the payment can be sent now, why not if it can't, the fee, the approval needed, and simulations and gas estimates for each step. It reserves nothing: another payment can still use the balance, the daily budget or the allowance. A wallet payment's last step can't be simulated before its schedule and approval exist, so its gas is an estimate, not a measurement.

`prepare()` refuses a payment that can't be sent, and returns input with the token, the policy and `maxDebit` fixed, and `startBy` set to when the quote expires.

## Deadlines

- `startBy`: the payment must start before this time. Once it has started, a retry continues it at any time: a payment that went through is reported as paid, never as expired.
- `validUntil`: the payment must land before this time.
  - From a wallet, the schedule expires a second earlier, so the contract refuses a late payment.
  - From a policy, nothing is broadcast in the last 30 seconds; a payment still unsent then is cancelled at its nonce, as above.
  - Neither starts within minutes of the deadline. A retry can't change it.

A payment cancelled or expired this way is reported as not paid only once that is certain, as a `refused` error with `details.expired` or `details.cancelled`. Then, and only then, a new key may pay again.

## Sign an invoice

A signed invoice is the recipient's EIP-712 signature over the exact payer, recipient, token, amount, order id, a random nonce, and when it was issued and expires. The payer can check it was signed by the recipient before paying.

`create()` also creates a backend request with the same terms and signs it. `sign()` signs without one.

```ts
const invoice = await receiver.invoices.create({
  payer: payer.address,
  amount: "1",
  token: "USDT",
  orderId: "order-123",
  expiresAt: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600,
});

const terms = await payer.invoices.verify(invoice);
const sent = await payer.invoices.pay(invoice, {
  funding: "wallet",
  maxDebit: "1.01",
});
console.log(terms.id, sent.status, sent.hash);
```

For policy funding the invoice names the policy owner as the payer, and the agent pays with `invoices.pay(invoice, { funding: "policy", policyId })`.

`pay` quotes the payment before anything else, and refuses one that can't be made now or that would debit more than `maxDebit`. It then reserves the invoice for this payment route, signer and key, so no other route can pay it as well. A retry after the invoice expired still reports a payment made while it was valid. Keep that reservation after a payment whose outcome is uncertain. The default reservation store is memory; workers share the Postgres one.

An invoice made with `sign()` and no request is tied to its payment only by the payment's memo, which carries `invoiceReference(invoice id)`. A schedule's payment has no memo, so such an invoice is paid from a policy; to pay from a wallet, make the invoice with `create()`.

### Verify the payment

```ts
import type { SignedInvoice } from "remesso-sdk";
import type { Hex } from "viem";

declare const invoice: SignedInvoice;
declare const paymentHash: Hex;
const evidence = await receiver.invoices.verifyPayment(invoice, {
  txHash: paymentHash,
  scheduleId,
  finality: "finalized",
});
console.log(evidence.invoiceId, evidence.orderId, evidence.payment.eventId);
```

Pass `policyId` instead of `scheduleId` for a policy payment. `verifyPayment` checks the payment against the invoice's exact terms, and that it is this invoice's payment:
- with a request, the policy payment carries the request's reference, or the schedule is the one the request was answered with;
- without one, the policy payment carries `invoiceReference`. A subscription's payment of the same amount doesn't count.

It also checks that the payment landed while the invoice was valid; it can confirm an expired invoice that was paid in time. It is finalized by default and refuses while the RPC can't say whether the block is final.

### Fulfil each order once

Commit the fulfilment and its deduplication together. The Postgres inbox refuses a payment, an invoice or an order that was already fulfilled:

```ts
import type { SignedInvoice } from "remesso-sdk";
import { createPostgresStorage } from "remesso-sdk/postgres";
import type { Hex } from "viem";

declare const storage: ReturnType<typeof createPostgresStorage>;
declare const invoice: SignedInvoice;
declare const paymentHash: Hex;
const terms = await receiver.invoices.verify(invoice, { allowExpired: true });
const verified = await receiver.invoices.verifyPayment(invoice, {
  txHash: paymentHash, scheduleId, finality: "finalized",
});
await storage.inbox.processOnce({
  eventId: verified.payment.eventId,
  invoiceId: verified.invoiceId,
  issuer: terms.issuer,
  orderId: terms.orderId,
}, async (tx) => {
  await tx.unsafe(
    "update orders set paid_at = clock_timestamp() where issuer = $1 and id = $2",
    [terms.issuer.toLowerCase(), terms.orderId],
  );
  // Insert an outbox row here for emails, shipping or calls to other services.
});
```

Make every business write through `tx`: if the callback throws, the claim and the writes roll back together. An email or an HTTP call can't roll back, so queue those in an outbox in the same transaction.

## Recover payments after a crash

```ts
const operation = await agent.remittances.get("order-123", { funding: "wallet" });
console.log(operation.status, operation.stage, operation.error);

const pending = await agent.remittances.listPending();
await agent.remittances.reconcile("order-123", { funding: "wallet", waitMs: 30_000 });
const recovered = await agent.remittances.recoverPending({ limit: 25, waitMs: 5_000 });
console.log(pending.length, recovered.length);
```

`get()` and `listPending()` only read: the saved payment and what the chain says about it. `listPending()` leaves out payments that settled more than two hours ago. `reconcile()` and `recoverPending()` continue payments that have started: they send saved transactions, and finish a wallet payment's remaining steps. They never start a payment, and never start a new one under an old key. A payment saved but never signed, for example because signing failed, is left for its own caller to retry.

The statuses are `prepared`, `awaiting_approval`, `signed`, `broadcast`, `included`, `finalized`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `paused`, `expired` and `needs_reconciliation`. A wallet payment whose step reverted while its schedule is still live is `needs_reconciliation`, not `failed`: it could still be paid, and reconciling cancels it. A transaction whose nonce was used by something else, with no receipt to show what, also needs a person to look at its hash; the SDK never pays it again.

`recoverPending()` makes one pass, over 25 payments by default; run it from your own scheduler. If a key exists in both journals, pass `funding`.

```ts
const settled = await agent.remittances.wait("order-123", {
  funding: "wallet",
  finality: "finalized",
  timeoutMs: 30 * 60_000,
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30 * 60_000),
});
console.log(settled.proof?.eventId);
```

`wait()` only watches. It throws for a payment that failed, was cancelled, paused or expired.

### Jobs

`storage.jobs` is a queue for your own work: enqueue under a key that never changes, claim with `SKIP LOCKED`, and acknowledge with the claim's token. A job is delivered at least once, so use its key as the payment's idempotency key. A claim lasts five minutes by default, longer than a payment's wait; renew it with `extend` for longer work. Payment keys belong to one signing key, so the workers that take payment jobs must all sign with the same key.

## Managed signers

A key held by a custody service plugs in through callbacks that sign and never broadcast:

```ts
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import {
  managedSigner,
  type ManagedTransactionRequest,
  type ManagedTypedDataRequest,
} from "remesso-sdk/signers";
import type { Address, Hex } from "viem";

declare const provider: {
  address: Address;
  signTransaction(request: ManagedTransactionRequest): Promise<Hex>;
  signTypedData(request: ManagedTypedDataRequest): Promise<Hex>;
};
const account = managedSigner({
  address: provider.address,
  signTransaction: (request) => provider.signTransaction(request),
  signTypedData: (request) => provider.signTypedData(request),
});
const agent = createRemesso({ account }); // In production, add the shared journals above.
```

The SDK passes the exact transaction, its Celo encoding and its hash, including a fee currency. It refuses anything back that differs: other fields, another signer, or a high-s signature, which Celo nodes reject. The SDK keeps simulation, journaling, nonces and broadcasting. No custody provider has been tested with it yet.

## Agent tools

`remesso-sdk/tools` gives an agent framework tools with JSON schemas and structured results. They return no wallet objects or signed bytes, and a URL in an error keeps only its host. Tools that pay are off by default:

```ts
import { createAgentTools } from "remesso-sdk/tools";

const tools = createAgentTools(agent);
console.log(tools.list());
const result = await tools.call("remesso_quote", {
  funding: "wallet", to: receiver.address, amount: "1", token: "USDT",
});
console.log(result);
```

Allow a payment from your own records of what was ordered and approved, with `authorizeWrite({ name, input })`; text from a model or a tool description is never permission to spend. `enableWrites: true` is for hosts that already check this themselves. When a payment's outcome is uncertain, the tool says so: reconcile its key rather than making a new one.

The repository's MCP server uses these tools and the same journals. Its tools that pay stay off unless the host sets `REMESSO_ENABLE_AGENT_TOOLS_WRITES=1`:

```bash
npm --prefix mcp install
npm --prefix mcp run build
npm --prefix mcp start
```

---

# Pay on a schedule

> Create a schedule the payer signs once, read it back, and pause, resume or cancel it.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules

A schedule is a payment the payer signs once: a fixed amount, to a fixed address, on a fixed cadence. Remesso's executor sends each payment when it is due. This page covers creating a schedule with the SDK, checking on it, and managing it afterwards.

After signing, nothing can change the recipient, the amount or the cadence: not Remesso, not the contract's owner, not the payer. The payer can pause, resume or cancel. Cancelling is the only edit.

## Before you start

You need:

- a client with an account that holds the token you pay in. See [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation).
- gas for two transactions, an approval and the schedule itself. CELO works for every token. With no CELO, USDT, USDC, USDm and USA₮ can pay their own gas. See [Fees, limits and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas).
- at least the executor's minimum per payment: the equivalent of 1 US dollar, such as 1 USDT or 1,500 wARS.

## Create a schedule

`schedules.create` approves the contract for the schedule's total, creates the schedule, and returns its id. This program pays 5 USDT a month, twelve times:

```ts title="pay-monthly.ts"
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const payer = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PAYER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

const s = await payer.schedules.create({
  to: process.env.RECIPIENT!,
  amount: "5",
  token: "USDT",
  every: "month",
  runs: 12,
});

console.log(`schedule ${s.id}: ${formatAmount(s.recipientGets, s.token)} arrives each month`);
console.log(`approval ${s.approveHash}, schedule ${s.hash}`);
for (const w of s.warnings) console.warn(w);
```

Two transactions go out, in order:

1. **An approval.** The SDK adds this schedule's total (here 60 USDT) to the approval you have already given the contract. It never replaces it, because another schedule may rely on it. Pass `approve: false` if you manage approvals yourself.
2. **The schedule.** The SDK reads its id from the transaction's own `ScheduleCreated` log.

Before either is signed, the SDK checks everything the contract or the executor would refuse. See [What the SDK refuses before signing](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules#what-the-sdk-refuses-before-signing).

### Options

| Option | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | Yes, unless `request` gives it | The recipient's address. |
| `amount` | One of `amount` or `receive` | What leaves your wallet each payment, as a decimal string: `"1.50"`. |
| `receive` | One of `amount` or `receive` | What the recipient receives each payment, after the fee. The SDK works out what to send. |
| `token` | No | A symbol or an address. Default `USDT`, or the request's token. |
| `every` | No | `"week"`, `"fortnight"`, `"month"`, `"quarter"`, or a number of seconds, at least 3,600. Default `"week"`, or the request's cadence. |
| `runs` | Yes, unless `request` gives it | How many payments. |
| `firstRunAt` | No | A `Date` for the first payment. Default: now. |
| `trigger` | No | Who may bring a payment forward: `"remesso"` or an address. Default: nobody. |
| `triggers` | No | How many early sends the trigger may make. Default: one per payment. |
| `request` | No | The id of a payment request this schedule answers. Its terms fill whatever you leave out. |
| `approve` | No | `false` to skip the approval. Default: approve this schedule's total on top of what is already approved. |

## Send an amount, or make an amount arrive

The 0.25% fee comes out of each payment. Choose which side of it you fix:

```ts
// 1 USDT leaves your wallet. The recipient receives 0.9975 USDT.
await payer.schedules.create({ to: "0xRecipient", amount: "1", token: "USDT", every: "week", runs: 4 });

// 1 USDT arrives. Your wallet sends 1.002507 USDT.
await payer.schedules.create({ to: "0xRecipient", receive: "1", token: "USDT", every: "week", runs: 4 });
```

Use `receive` when the recipient is owed an exact amount, such as an invoice. The per-payment limits apply to what leaves your wallet in both cases. [Fees, limits and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas) shows the arithmetic.

## Choose the cadence and the first payment

`every` takes a cadence name or a number of seconds:

| `every` | Interval |
|---|---|
| `"week"` | 7 days |
| `"fortnight"` | 14 days |
| `"month"` | 30 days |
| `"quarter"` | 90 days |
| a number | that many seconds, at least 3,600 |

`"weekly"`, `"monthly"` and the other `-ly` forms are accepted too. A month is always 30 days, as in the Remesso app.

```ts
// Every three days, ten times.
await payer.schedules.create({ to: "0xRecipient", amount: "20", every: 3 * 86_400, runs: 10 });

// Monthly in USDC, the first payment a week from now.
await payer.schedules.create({
  to: "0xRecipient",
  amount: "250",
  token: "USDC",
  every: "month",
  runs: 6,
  firstRunAt: new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 86_400_000),
});
```

A schedule lasts at most a year. The SDK sets its expiry to one interval and an hour after the last payment's slot, so `runs` payments must fit within 365 days: 12 monthly payments or 52 weekly ones fit, 13 monthly ones don't. For longer arrangements, create a new schedule before the old one ends.

`firstRunAt` can't be in the past.

## What you get back

`create` returns a `CreatedSchedule`:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `id` | The schedule's id on the contract, a `bigint`. |
| `hash` | The `createSchedule` transaction. |
| `approveHash` | The approval transaction, or `null` with `approve: false`. |
| `to`, `token` | The recipient, checksummed, and the token's symbol. |
| `amountIn` | What leaves your wallet each payment, in base units. |
| `recipientGets` | What the recipient receives each payment, in base units, after the fee. |
| `feeBps` | The commission this schedule pinned, in basis points (25 is 0.25%). |
| `runs`, `intervalSeconds` | How many payments, and how far apart. |
| `firstRunAt`, `expiresAt` | When the first payment is due, and when the schedule ends. |
| `request` | With `request`: how the request took the answer (`status` and `signed`), or `error`. |
| `warnings` | Things to fix that didn't stop the schedule, such as a balance below one payment. |

Check `warnings`. A schedule whose payer can't cover a payment is valid, and each payment fails until the wallet is funded.

## When the first payment goes out

The first payment is due at `firstRunAt`, which is now unless you set it. Remesso's executor sends due payments every minute. It learns about schedules created outside the Remesso app through a sync that reads the contract every five minutes. So the sync finds a new schedule within about five minutes, and its first payment goes out within a minute of that.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Payer as Your code
  participant Contract as RemessoExecutorV5
  participant Remesso as Remesso's executor
  participant Recipient
  Payer->>Contract: approve, then createSchedule (signed once)
  Remesso->>Contract: finds the schedule (within about 5 minutes)
  loop Each time a payment is due
    Remesso->>Contract: executeRun(id)
    Contract->>Recipient: the amount, less the 0.25% fee
  end
```

After that:

- **Each payment is due one interval after the previous one actually went out.** The cadence is measured from the payment, not from the original timetable.
- **Missed payments aren't caught up.** If a payment can't go, because the wallet is short, the approval is too low or the schedule is paused, it stays due and is retried. When it does go, the next one is due an interval later. A payer is never charged for two periods at once.
- **The schedule stops** after `runs` payments, at its expiry, or when it is cancelled.

To know when a payment arrived, watch [payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events) or receive [webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks).

## Let a payment be sent early

A trigger may bring one payment forward, ahead of its date. Grant it when you create the schedule:

```ts
const s = await payer.schedules.create({
  to: "0xRecipient",
  amount: "10",
  every: "month",
  runs: 12,
  trigger: "remesso", // Remesso's executor, whichever key it is at the time
  triggers: 3, // at most three early sends
});

await payer.schedules.setTrigger(s.id, "remesso", 1); // one early send left
await payer.schedules.setTrigger(s.id, null); // nobody can send early any more
```

`trigger` is `"remesso"` or an address:

- `"remesso"` stores Remesso's sentinel address, `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001`. It means whichever key is Remesso's executor at the time, so a key rotation moves the grant. Anyone can then pay 0.01 USDC, USDT or USA₮ over x402 to `trigger-run` and have Remesso send one payment early. See the [HTTP API](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/http-api).
- An address, such as your own agent's, lets that key call `runNow` on the contract itself and pay the gas.

An early send can't change the recipient or the amount, and it doesn't add a payment. It uses up the next one: if a payment is due next week and is sent today, the one after keeps its own date. Early sends are at most one a minute, never past the expiry, and stop when the count runs out. Sending a payment that is already due uses no count.

`setTrigger` takes the count as its third argument, and it defaults to 0, so pass a count whenever you grant a trigger.

A schedule created through the SDK is found by Remesso's sync within about five minutes. Until then, only a trigger can move it. `trigger: "remesso"` lets a first payment go out without waiting for the sync.

## Answer a payment request

When someone has sent you a [payment request](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests), create the schedule from it. Its terms fill everything you leave out, and the SDK reports the schedule against the request:

```ts
const s = await payer.schedules.create({ request: requestId });
if (s.request && "status" in s.request) console.log("the request reads", s.request.status);
else console.log("created, but not reported against the request:", s.request?.error);
```

The request's amount is what the recipient receives, so the SDK sends the amount plus the fee. The SDK refuses the request if it was sent to a different wallet, if it is no longer pending, or if you pass a `to` it didn't ask for. If reporting fails after the schedule is created, `create` still returns the schedule, with the reason in `s.request.error`.

## Read a schedule back

```ts
import { formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";

const s = await payer.schedules.get(scheduleId);
console.log(`${s.runsExecuted} of ${s.maxRuns} paid, next due ${s.nextRunAt.toISOString()}`);
console.log(`${formatAmount(s.recipientGets, s.token)} arrives each time`);

const { due, funded, approved } = await payer.schedules.status(scheduleId);
if (due && !funded) console.warn("a payment is due and the wallet holds less than one payment");
if (!approved) console.warn("the approval is below one payment: approve the contract again");

const ids = await payer.schedules.list(); // every schedule this wallet created
```

- **`get(id)`** returns the schedule as the contract stores it: `sender`, `to`, `token`, `amountIn`, `recipientGets`, `feeBps`, `intervalSeconds`, `maxRuns`, `runsExecuted`, `nextRunAt`, `lastRunAt`, `expiresAt`, `active`, `cancelled`, `trigger` and `triggersLeft`. Right after a schedule is created, a node can still answer from an earlier block, so `get` keeps asking for a few seconds. An id that doesn't exist throws [`not_found`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#not_found).
- **`status(id)`** asks the contract whether a payment can go now. `due` means a payment is due and the schedule is active, unexpired and not finished. `funded` means the payer's balance covers one payment, and `approved` means the approval does.
- **`list(sender?)`** returns the ids of every schedule a sender has created, by default this account's. A read-only client can pass any address.

## Pause, resume or cancel

Only the wallet that created a schedule can change it.

```ts
await payer.schedules.setActive(scheduleId, false); // pause
await payer.schedules.setActive(scheduleId, true); // resume
await payer.schedules.cancel(scheduleId); // for good
```

- **Pausing** stops payments until you resume. Payments that fall due while it is paused aren't caught up: after you resume, the due payment goes out and the cadence restarts from it.
- **Cancelling** is permanent. A cancelled schedule can't be resumed. Create a new one instead.
- **The approval stays** after a cancel. Lower it yourself if nothing else needs it. Revoking the token approval also stops every future payment from that token, which is the backstop if you can't reach the contract.

Each of these is a transaction. It pays gas in CELO, or in the schedule's token if you hold no CELO and the token can pay gas.

## What the SDK refuses before signing

Each refusal is a [`RemessoError`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors) with a `code`, thrown before anything is signed:

| Situation | Code |
|---|---|
| `to` is missing or isn't an address | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| `to` is your own wallet: a schedule paying itself only loses the fee | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| Both `amount` and `receive`, or neither | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| `runs` is missing or not a whole number | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| `every` is under 3,600 seconds, or not a cadence name | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| `firstRunAt` is in the past | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| The token isn't one Remesso knows | [`invalid`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#invalid) |
| The contract doesn't take the token for new schedules | [`refused`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#refused) |
| The amount is outside the executor's per-payment range | [`refused`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#refused) |
| The payments don't fit in a year | [`refused`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#refused) |
| The request was sent to another wallet, isn't pending, or asks for another `to` | [`refused`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#refused) |
| The RPC isn't Celo mainnet | [`wrong_chain`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#wrong_chain) |
| The client has no account | [`no_account`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#no_account) |
| Neither CELO nor the token can pay the gas | [`no_gas`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#no_gas) |

The SDK also simulates each transaction first, and a refusal from the contract arrives as `refused` with the contract's reason in words. A transaction that is mined and then reverts throws [`reverted`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#reverted): nothing moved.

The per-payment range matters most. A schedule outside it is valid on-chain and would never run, because the executor won't send it:

```ts
import { RemessoError } from "remesso-sdk";

try {
  await payer.schedules.create({ to: "0xRecipient", amount: "0.50", token: "USDT", every: "week", runs: 4 });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof RemessoError && e.code === "refused") console.error(e.message); // under the 1 USDT minimum
  else throw e;
}
```

## Next steps

- [Payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events) and [webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks): know when each payment arrives.
- [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests): let the recipient ask for the schedule.
- [Fees, limits and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas): what each payment costs, and every token's range.
