# Subscriptions for your app

> Bill each customer monthly in stablecoins, grant access when a payment arrives, and notice when a customer pauses or cancels.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/subscriptions

You run a SaaS or an API product and want customers to pay monthly in stablecoins. Card-style billing, where you charge the customer, doesn't exist here: Remesso can't take money from anyone. Instead, each customer signs a mandate once: a fixed amount, to your address, every month, for a set number of payments. Remesso's executor then sends each payment when it's due. Your app asks for the mandate, then reacts to the payments.

## What you'll build

- **Checkout:** a payment request per customer, and the link that opens their Remesso form filled in.
- **A webhook** that grants access when a payment arrives, records it once it's final, and takes it back if a reorg undoes it.
- **A daily check** that notices a cancelled, paused or underfunded subscription. Webhooks announce payments only, so this is how you learn about everything else.

## What Remesso does and doesn't do

Be clear with yourself, and with your customers, about the model:

- **The customer is in control.** They can pause or cancel the schedule at any time, from the Remesso app or their own code. You can't charge them, extend the schedule or change its amount.
- **Terms are fixed at signing.** A new price means a new schedule: send a new request, and the customer cancels the old schedule (only they can).
- **A schedule has an end.** It lasts at most a year, so 12 monthly payments. Renew with a new request before the last one.
- **A month is 30 days.** Payment dates drift against calendar months by a day or so each month.
- **There are no refunds in the protocol.** A refund is a transfer you send yourself.
- **A late payment still goes out.** If a payment is due while the customer's wallet is short, or their approval is too low, it waits. It goes out once it can, as long as the schedule hasn't expired.

## Prerequisites

- The setup from [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation), and a key for your app's receiving address. Receiving needs no gas and no balance. The key signs your webhook subscription and nothing else.
- A public HTTPS URL for the webhook. For a test, `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8787` prints one.
- Each customer needs USDT on Celo for each payment plus the 0.25% fee, and a little CELO to sign the schedule once.

```bash
export APP_KEY=0x… PUBLIC_URL=https://….trycloudflare.com
```

## Step 1: Ask at checkout

Create one request per customer, and keep its id next to the customer. The amount is what you receive each month: the customer's form adds the fee on top.

```ts title="checkout.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const app = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.APP_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

/// At checkout: ask the customer's wallet to pay for the plan every month.
/// Returns the link to show them. It opens their Remesso form, filled in.
export async function startSubscription(customerId: string, customerWallet: string): Promise<string> {
  const req = await app.requests.create({
    payer: customerWallet,
    amount: "10", // USDT a month: what you receive
    token: "USDT",
    every: "month",
    runs: 12,
    from: "Example API", // up to 40 characters
    note: "Pro plan, billed monthly", // up to 120 characters
  });
  await saveSubscription({ customerId, requestId: req.id });
  return req.link;
}

async function saveSubscription(row: { customerId: string; requestId: string }): Promise<void> {
  // Your database: remember which request belongs to which customer.
}
```

The request also appears in the customer's Remesso inbox. A request stays open for 30 days, and a wallet can have at most 10 open requests at a time.

When the customer signs, the request reads `accepted`. Don't grant access yet: accepted isn't paid. Access follows the first payment.

## Step 2: Grant access on each payment

Each payment produces up to three deliveries to your webhook:

| Delivery | What your app does |
|---|---|
| `payment.received` | Grant access until the next payment is due, plus a grace period. |
| `payment.finalized` | Record the payment as final, for your accounts. It follows 25 to 30 minutes later. |
| `payment.removed` | Take that period's access back: a reorg undid the payment. This is rare. |

A delivery names the schedule, not the customer. The first time a schedule appears, find the request it answers, and remember the pairing.

```ts title="webhook.ts"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createRemesso, webhookHandler, type WebhookMessage } from "remesso-sdk";
import { toNodeListener } from "remesso-sdk/node";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const app = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.APP_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
const PERIOD_MS = 30 * 86_400_000; // a Remesso month is 30 days
const GRACE_MS = 3 * 86_400_000;

async function onPayment(m: WebhookMessage) {
  if (!m.data.schedule || (await alreadyHandled(m.id))) return; // retries reuse the webhook-id
  const customerId = await customerFor(m.data.schedule);
  if (!customerId) return; // a payment that isn't a subscription
  if (m.type === "payment.received") {
    await grantAccess(customerId, new Date(Date.parse(m.data.blockTime) + PERIOD_MS + GRACE_MS));
  } else if (m.type === "payment.finalized") {
    await recordFinal(customerId, m.data.txHash);
  } else {
    await revokePayment(customerId, m.data.txHash);
  }
  await markHandled(m.id);
}

/// Which customer a schedule pays for, found once through the request it answers.
async function customerFor(scheduleId: string): Promise<string | null> {
  for (const sub of await openSubscriptions()) {
    if (sub.scheduleId === scheduleId) return sub.customerId;
    if (sub.scheduleId) continue;
    const r = await app.requests.get(sub.requestId);
    if (r.payment?.schedule?.id === scheduleId) {
      await saveScheduleId(sub.customerId, scheduleId);
      return sub.customerId;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

// Your database and your app. These stand in for them.
async function openSubscriptions(): Promise<{ customerId: string; requestId: string; scheduleId?: string }[]> {
  return [];
}
async function saveScheduleId(customerId: string, scheduleId: string): Promise<void> {}
async function grantAccess(customerId: string, until: Date): Promise<void> {}
async function recordFinal(customerId: string, txHash: string): Promise<void> {}
async function revokePayment(customerId: string, txHash: string): Promise<void> {}
async function alreadyHandled(webhookId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return false;
}
async function markHandled(webhookId: string): Promise<void> {}

let secret = process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET; // saved from the first subscribe
const handler = webhookHandler({ recipient: app.address, secret: () => secret, onPayment });
createServer(toNodeListener(handler)).listen(8787);

if (!secret) {
  secret = (await app.webhooks.subscribe({ url: process.env.PUBLIC_URL! })).secret;
  console.log("Store this signing secret as WEBHOOK_SECRET:", secret);
}
```

If `onPayment` throws, the handler answers 500 and Remesso retries with the same `webhook-id` for 24 hours. That makes an outage of your database safe: nothing is lost, it just arrives later.

## Step 3: Check each subscription daily

Webhooks tell you about payments, not about a customer pausing or cancelling. Read each schedule from the contract once a day. Reading needs no key.

```ts title="check.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";

const reader = createRemesso(); // reading schedules needs no key

type State = "active" | "payment waiting" | "paused" | "cancelled" | "completed";

/// What a customer's schedule says now, read from the contract.
async function stateOf(scheduleId: string): Promise<State> {
  const [s, run] = await Promise.all([reader.schedules.get(scheduleId), reader.schedules.status(scheduleId)]);
  if (s.cancelled) return "cancelled";
  // The contract turns `active` off on the last payment too, so count first.
  if (s.runsExecuted >= s.maxRuns || s.expiresAt < new Date()) return "completed";
  if (!s.active) return "paused";
  if (run.due && !(run.funded && run.approved)) return "payment waiting";
  return "active";
}

for (const sub of await subscriptionsWithSchedules()) {
  const state = await stateOf(sub.scheduleId);
  if (state !== "active") await tellCustomer(sub.customerId, state);
}

// Your database and your app. These stand in for them.
async function subscriptionsWithSchedules(): Promise<{ customerId: string; scheduleId: string }[]> {
  return [];
}
async function tellCustomer(customerId: string, state: State): Promise<void> {
  // "payment waiting": ask them to top up their wallet, or raise their approval.
  // "completed": send a new request to renew.
}
```

`schedules.status` reads the contract's own view of the next payment: whether it's due, and whether the customer's balance (`funded`) and approval (`approved`) cover it.

## Test it safely

1. Use a second wallet you control as the customer, holding about 1.01 USDT and a little CELO.
2. In `checkout.ts`, ask for `amount: "1"` with `runs: 1`. One USDT is the smallest payment the executor sends.
3. Start `webhook.ts`, then sign from the customer wallet using the link.
4. Watch `payment.received` arrive within a few minutes, then `payment.finalized`. Run `check.ts` afterwards: the schedule reads `completed`.

## Where to go next

- [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests): request states, and what a payer sees.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks): the challenge, rotating the secret, and replaying failed deliveries.
- [Schedules](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules): reading, pausing and cancelling schedules.
- [Webhook payloads](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/webhook-payloads): every field of a delivery.

---

# Pay a team on a schedule

> Sign one schedule per contractor so each receives an exact monthly amount, budget the total, check funding before payday, and stop a schedule when a contract ends.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/payroll

A small company pays its contractors every month in USDT. The work is repetitive: send each payment, get the amount right after fees, and check the money is there before payday. With Remesso the employer signs one schedule per contractor, once. Each person then receives the exact amount you name every month, and you only watch that the wallet stays funded.

The same steps work for an employer's agent, running on the employer's key.

## What you'll build

- `payroll.ts` budgets the team's pay, checks the wallet can cover the first payday, and signs one schedule per contractor.
- `before-payday.ts` checks every schedule's next payment is funded and approved.
- A one-line cancel for when a contract ends.

## Prerequisites

- The setup from [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation), and the employer's key. It holds the USDT and signs each schedule.
- A little CELO for gas: about 0.05 CELO per contractor, for an approval and a schedule. With no CELO, the SDK pays gas in USDT.
- Each contractor's wallet address. Receiving needs no gas and no balance. MiniPay shows USDT, so a contractor can use it.

```bash
export EMPLOYER_KEY=0x…
```

## Limits that shape a payroll

- **Each payment is 1 to 1,000 USDT before the fee.** After the 0.25% fee, a contractor can receive at most 997.50 USDT per payment. The SDK refuses anything outside that before signing. Other tokens have their own bounds: see [Tokens and limits](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/tokens-and-limits).
- **A schedule lasts at most a year from signing.** With the first payday up to a month away, six monthly payments fit comfortably. Sign again for the next six. The SDK refuses a schedule whose payments don't fit.
- **A month is 30 days.** Paydays drift against calendar dates, by a day or so each month.
- **Each schedule is its own approval.** For every contractor the SDK sends two transactions: it adds that schedule's total to your USDT approval for the contract, then creates the schedule. The approval is the most that schedule can ever take.

## Step 1: Budget and sign

Use `receive` so each contractor gets exactly the amount you name. The SDK adds the fee on top. `grossFor` does the same sum, so you can budget before signing anything.

```ts title="payroll.ts"
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createRemesso, erc20Abi, FEE_BPS, formatAmount, grossFor, token, toUnits } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const employer = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.EMPLOYER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
const usdt = token("USDT");

/// Who gets paid, and what arrives each month after the fee.
const team = [
  { name: "Designer", wallet: "0xDesignerWallet", receive: "400" },
  { name: "Developer", wallet: "0xDeveloperWallet", receive: "650" },
];
const runs = 6; // six months: sign again for the next six

// What leaves your wallet each payday, and in all.
const perPayday = team.reduce((sum, p) => sum + grossFor(toUnits(p.receive, usdt), FEE_BPS), 0n);
const balance = await employer.publicClient.readContract({
  address: usdt.address,
  abi: erc20Abi,
  functionName: "balanceOf",
  args: [employer.address],
});
console.log(`each payday: ${formatAmount(perPayday, usdt)}; over ${runs} months: ${formatAmount(perPayday * BigInt(runs), usdt)}`);
if (balance < perPayday) throw new Error(`the wallet holds ${formatAmount(balance, usdt)}: not enough for the first payday`);

// The first payday: 09:00 UTC on the 1st of next month.
const now = new Date();
const payday = new Date(Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth() + 1, 1, 9));

const ids: Record<string, string> = {};
for (const p of team) {
  const s = await employer.schedules.create({
    to: p.wallet,
    receive: p.receive,
    token: "USDT",
    every: "month",
    runs,
    firstRunAt: payday,
  });
  ids[p.name] = s.id.toString();
  console.log(`${p.name}: schedule #${s.id}, ${formatAmount(s.recipientGets, usdt)} a month from ${s.firstRunAt.toDateString()}`);
  for (const w of s.warnings) console.log(`  note: ${w}`);
}
await writeFile("payroll.json", JSON.stringify(ids, null, 2));
```

The wallet doesn't need the whole six months up front. Each payment is taken when it's due, so the balance only has to cover each payday as it comes.

## Step 2: Check before each payday

One balance pays every schedule. `schedules.status` tells you whether the next payment of each schedule is covered on its own. The total check makes sure the balance covers everyone paid the same day.

```ts title="before-payday.ts"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createRemesso, erc20Abi, formatAmount, token } from "remesso-sdk";

const reader = createRemesso(); // reading needs no key
const usdt = token("USDT");
const employer = process.env.EMPLOYER as `0x${string}`; // the employer's address
const ids = JSON.parse(await readFile("payroll.json", "utf8")) as Record<string, string>;

const soon = Date.now() + 2 * 86_400_000;
let dueSoon = 0n;
for (const [name, id] of Object.entries(ids)) {
  const [s, run] = await Promise.all([reader.schedules.get(id), reader.schedules.status(id)]);
  if (s.cancelled || s.runsExecuted >= s.maxRuns) continue; // stopped, or done
  if (run.nextRunAt.getTime() < soon) dueSoon += s.amountIn;
  const problems = [
    !s.active && "paused",
    !run.funded && "the balance is below one payment",
    !run.approved && "the approval is below one payment",
  ].filter(Boolean);
  console.log(`${name} #${id}: next payment ${run.nextRunAt.toDateString()}${problems.length ? `, PROBLEM: ${problems.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
}

const balance = await reader.publicClient.readContract({
  address: usdt.address,
  abi: erc20Abi,
  functionName: "balanceOf",
  args: [employer],
});
if (balance < dueSoon) console.log(`top up: ${formatAmount(dueSoon, usdt)} is due in the next two days, and the wallet holds ${formatAmount(balance, usdt)}`);
```

A payment that's due when the wallet is short doesn't fail for good. It waits, and goes out once the wallet is topped up, as long as the schedule hasn't expired.

## Step 3: When a contract changes or ends

Terms are fixed at signing. To pay someone a different amount, cancel their schedule and sign a new one. To stop paying, cancel:

```ts
await payer.schedules.cancel(scheduleId); // stops every future payment
```

Only the wallet that signed a schedule can cancel it. Cancelling leaves your token approval as it is: if nothing else needs it, lower it with an ordinary ERC-20 `approve` from your wallet.

For a break, such as unpaid leave, pause instead and resume later:

```ts
await payer.schedules.setActive(scheduleId, false); // pause
await payer.schedules.setActive(scheduleId, true); // resume
```

## Test it safely

1. Put one contractor in `team`: a second wallet you control, with `receive: "1"`.
2. Set `runs = 1` and leave out `firstRunAt`, so the payment is due at once.
3. Give the employer wallet about 1.01 USDT and a little CELO, then run `payroll.ts`.
4. A schedule created from code is found by Remesso within about five minutes, and paid within a minute of that. Run `before-payday.ts` before and after.

## Where to go next

- [Schedules](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules): every option of `create`, and reading, pausing and cancelling.
- [Fees and gas](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/fees-and-gas): `grossFor`, `netOf` and who pays gas when.
- [Payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events): a record of every payment for your accounts.

---

# Send money home every month

> Pay a family member in USDT every month from one signature, and tell them each time money arrives, with a link to cash it out.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/remittances

Someone working in London supports family in Lagos, and sends money every month. Each transfer means another form, another fee and another wait. With Remesso the sender signs once. After that, the family receives USDT every 30 days, in a wallet they already use, such as MiniPay, and a short program tells them each time money arrives.

## What you'll build

- `send-home.ts` signs a monthly USDT schedule to a family member's wallet, so they receive an exact amount every month.
- `notify.ts` watches for each payment and sends the family a message with the amount and a link to cash it out.

## Choose the token

The family's wallet and their way to cash out decide the token:

- **In MiniPay, pay USDT, USDC, USDm or USA₮.** MiniPay shows only those four. It doesn't show cNGN or Ripio's local-currency tokens: a recipient paid in those needs another wallet.
- **For naira, pay USDT.** On Celo, USDT is the token Textile pairs with cNGN. The recipient opens Textile with their own wallet, swaps USDT to cNGN, and uses "Withdraw NGN" to a Nigerian bank account in their own name: `https://app.textilecredit.com/s/swap?sell=USDT&buy=cNGN&chainId=42220`.
- **For pesos, reais or soles, pay the country's Ripio token:** wARS, wBRL, wCOP, wMXN, wCLP or wPEN. The recipient cashes out on Ripio's ramp, for example `https://ramp.ripio.com/off-ramp?country=AR&chain=42220&token=WARS` for Argentina, or `country=BR` with `token=WBRL` for Brazil. Which countries Ripio ramps on Celo is Ripio's to decide.

Remesso never pays into a bank account on the sender's behalf. The family receives tokens in their own wallet, and cashes them out themselves, if and when they choose.

## Prerequisites

- The setup from [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation), and the sender's key. It holds the USDT: each payment plus Remesso's 0.25% fee.
- A little CELO to sign the schedule once, about 0.05 CELO. With no CELO, the SDK pays the gas in USDT. Remesso's executor pays the gas of every monthly payment after that.
- The family member's wallet address. Receiving needs no gas, no balance and no software.

```bash
export SENDER_KEY=0x… FAMILY_WALLET=0x…
```

## Step 1: Sign the schedule

`receive` is what arrives each month. The SDK adds the fee to what leaves your wallet.

```ts title="send-home.ts"
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const payer = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.SENDER_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

const s = await payer.schedules.create({
  to: process.env.FAMILY_WALLET!,
  receive: "50", // USDT that arrives each month
  token: "USDT",
  every: "month",
  runs: 12, // a year: the longest a schedule lasts
});

console.log(`schedule #${s.id}: ${formatAmount(s.amountIn, "USDT")} leaves your wallet each month`);
console.log(`${formatAmount(s.recipientGets, "USDT")} arrives, ${s.runs} times, until ${s.expiresAt.toDateString()}`);
for (const w of s.warnings) console.log("note:", w);
```

This sends two transactions. The first adds the year's total to your USDT approval for the contract: that approval is the most the schedule can ever take. The second creates the schedule. Remesso finds a schedule created from code within about five minutes, and sends the first payment then. After that, payments go out every 30 days.

To start on a particular day, pass `firstRunAt`. A schedule lasts at most a year from signing, so a later start fits fewer payments: the SDK refuses a schedule whose payments don't fit, before signing anything.

The wallet doesn't need the whole year up front. Each payment is taken when it's due, so keep one month's payment and the fee in it. If it's short when a payment is due, that payment waits. It goes out once the wallet is topped up, as long as the schedule hasn't expired.

## Step 2: Tell the family each time

Payment events are public, so the watcher needs no key, and the family needs no software. This one tells them once each payment is final, about half an hour after it lands, so a message never has to be taken back.

```ts title="notify.ts"
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";

const reader = createRemesso(); // payment events are public: no key needed
const family = process.env.FAMILY_WALLET!;
const scheduleId = process.env.SCHEDULE_ID!; // printed by send-home.ts
const CASH_OUT = "https://app.textilecredit.com/s/swap?sell=USDT&buy=cNGN&chainId=42220";

// Where the last run stopped, so a restart doesn't announce a payment again.
const after = Number(await readFile("notify-seq.txt", "utf8").catch(() => "0"));

for await (const e of reader.events.watch({ address: family, role: "to", kinds: ["run"], after })) {
  if (e.refId === scheduleId && e.final && !e.removed) {
    await tell(`${formatAmount(e.amount!, e.token!)} has arrived. To cash it out to your bank account: ${CASH_OUT}`);
  }
  await writeFile("notify-seq.txt", String(e.seq)); // after telling: a crash repeats a message, never skips one
}

async function tell(message: string) {
  // Your messaging: SMS, WhatsApp, email. Printed here.
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), message);
}
```

Each event comes round again when it changes, so a payment appears once when it lands and again when it becomes final. Announcing only the final one sends exactly one message per payment. To tell the family sooner, announce events that aren't final yet too, and send a correction if one is later marked `removed`.

## Step 3: Change or stop

The schedule's recipient, amount and cadence are fixed once it's signed. Nobody can change them, Remesso included.

- **To send a different amount**, cancel and sign a new schedule.
- **If the family moves to a new wallet**, the schedule keeps paying the old one. Cancel it and sign a new one to the new address.
- **To stop**, cancel with the same client that signed. It stops every future payment:

```ts
await payer.schedules.cancel(scheduleId);
```

To skip a while without cancelling, pause with `schedules.setActive(scheduleId, false)`, and resume later with `true`.

## Test it safely

1. Use a second wallet you control as the family's wallet. A MiniPay wallet works, and shows the USDT arriving.
2. Sign with `receive: "1"` and `runs: 1`: about 1.0025 USDT leaves the sender's wallet.
3. Start `notify.ts` with the schedule id. The payment goes out within about five minutes, and the message follows once it's final, about half an hour later.

## Where to go next

- [Schedules](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/schedules): every option of `create`, and pausing and cancelling.
- [Payment events](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-events): paging, finality and reorgs.
- [Tokens and limits](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/tokens-and-limits): which tokens a schedule can pay, and the per-payment bounds.

---

# A weekly allowance, approved by an agent

> A child's agent asks a parent for cNGN every week; the parent's agent shows the request and signs a weekly schedule after a yes.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/family-allowance

A student in Lagos gets a weekly allowance from a parent, in naira. With Remesso, two agents handle it. The child's agent sends one payment request. The parent's agent shows it, asks the parent, and signs a weekly schedule on a yes. From then on, the allowance arrives every week, and the child's agent says so, with a link to cash it out to the child's own bank account.

## What you'll build

- `child.ts` asks the parent's wallet for a weekly amount of cNGN once, then listens for each payment by webhook.
- `parent.ts` lists the requests waiting for the parent's wallet, explains what signing would cost, and signs or declines.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Child's agent
    participant R as Remesso
    participant P as Parent's agent
    participant E as Executor
    C->>R: requests.create (cNGN, every week)
    P->>R: requests.list
    P->>P: shows it, and the parent says yes
    P->>R: schedules.create, answering the request
    E->>C: each week, the allowance
    R->>C: payment.received, then payment.finalized
```

## Prerequisites

- The setup from [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation), on both sides.
- **The child:** a key, and a wallet that shows cNGN. MiniPay doesn't. Receiving needs no gas and no balance. The child also needs a public HTTPS address that reaches port 8788: `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8788` prints one for a test.
- **The parent:** a key holding cNGN for each payment plus Remesso's 0.25% fee, and about 0.05 CELO to sign once. Textile swaps USDT into cNGN on Celo: `https://app.textilecredit.com/s/swap?sell=USDT&buy=cNGN&chainId=42220`.

cNGN is the Nigerian naira stablecoin, with 6 decimals. Remesso's executor sends 1,300 to 1,300,000 cNGN per payment.

## Step 1: The child asks, and listens

The child's agent asks once and saves the request, so a restart doesn't ask again. Then it serves the webhook. A payment counts only if it comes from the schedule that answers this request.

```ts title="child.ts"
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createRemesso, formatAmount, RemessoError, webhookHandler, type WebhookMessage } from "remesso-sdk";
import { toNodeListener } from "remesso-sdk/node";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const TEXTILE_WITHDRAW = "https://app.textilecredit.com/s/sell?chainId=42220";
const child = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.CHILD_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
const url = process.env.PUBLIC_URL!;

// Ask once. A restart reuses the saved request.
let saved = await readFile("allowance.json", "utf8").then((t) => JSON.parse(t) as { id: string }).catch(() => null);
if (!saved) {
  const req = await child.requests.create({
    payer: process.env.PARENT!,
    amount: process.env.AMOUNT ?? "1300", // cNGN a week: what you receive
    token: "cNGN",
    every: "week",
    runs: 12,
    from: "Your child",
    note: "Weekly allowance",
  });
  saved = { id: req.id };
  await writeFile("allowance.json", JSON.stringify(saved));
  console.log(`asked. If your parent prefers the Remesso app, this link opens the request: ${req.link}`);
}
const requestId = saved.id;

let secret: string | undefined;
const seen = new Set<string>();

async function onPayment(m: WebhookMessage) {
  if (seen.has(m.id) || !m.data.schedule) return;
  const r = await child.requests.get(requestId);
  if (!r.payment?.schedule) throw new Error("the allowance isn't answered yet"); // Remesso retries
  if (r.payment.schedule.id !== m.data.schedule) return; // some other payment to this wallet
  seen.add(m.id);
  const amount = formatAmount(m.data.amount, m.data.token);
  if (m.type === "payment.received") {
    console.log(`Allowance received: ${amount}, week ${m.data.runNumber}.`);
    console.log(`Cash it out to your own bank account on Textile ("Withdraw NGN"): ${TEXTILE_WITHDRAW}`);
  } else if (m.type === "payment.finalized") {
    console.log(`Week ${m.data.runNumber}: final.`);
  } else {
    console.log(`Week ${m.data.runNumber}'s payment was undone by a reorg. Nothing arrived: don't withdraw it.`);
  }
}

const server = createServer(toNodeListener(webhookHandler({ recipient: child.address, secret: () => secret, onPayment })));
await new Promise<void>((done) => server.listen(8788, done));
try {
  secret = (await child.webhooks.subscribe({ url })).secret;
} catch (e) {
  if (!(e instanceof RemessoError && e.code === "conflict")) throw e;
  secret = (await child.webhooks.rotate({ url })).secret; // subscribed before, and the secret is lost
}
console.log(`listening for the allowance at ${url}`);
```

Cashing out is Textile's "Withdraw NGN": the child withdraws from their own wallet to a bank account in their own name. Remesso pays out no naira itself.

## Step 2: The parent's agent asks, then signs

`requests.list()` returns the live requests sent to the parent's wallet: those still pending and under 30 days old. Before signing, the agent shows what the schedule will take. The child receives the amount asked, and the parent sends that plus the fee.

```ts title="parent.ts"
import { createInterface } from "node:readline/promises";
import { createRemesso, FEE_BPS, formatAmount, grossFor, token, toUnits } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const parent = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PARENT_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
const cngn = token("cNGN");

const [r] = (await parent.requests.list()).filter((x) => x.token === "cNGN" && x.amount && x.runs);
if (!r) {
  console.log("no cNGN requests are waiting");
  process.exit(0);
}

const each = grossFor(toUnits(r.amount!, cngn), FEE_BPS);
console.log(`${r.from ?? "Someone"} asks for ${r.amount} cNGN a week, ${r.runs} times: "${r.note ?? ""}"`);
console.log(`You'd send ${formatAmount(each, cngn)} a week, at most ${formatAmount(each * BigInt(r.runs!), cngn)} in all.`);

const ask = createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
const answer = (await ask.question("Sign it? [y/N] ")).trim().toLowerCase();
ask.close();

if (answer === "y") {
  const s = await parent.schedules.create({ request: r.id }); // the request's terms, the fee on top
  console.log(`schedule #${s.id} is live: https://celoscan.io/tx/${s.hash}`);
} else {
  await parent.requests.decline(r.id); // signed by this wallet: the child sees it declined
  console.log("declined");
}
```

Signing answers the request with its own terms. The SDK refuses a request addressed to a different wallet, or one that's no longer pending.

A decline is signed by the parent's wallet, so it holds for everyone: the child's `requests.get` then reads `declined`.

The schedule can't change once it's signed. The parent can pause it, resume it, or cancel it from the same client: `schedules.setActive(id, false)` and `schedules.cancel(id)`.

## Test it safely

1. Run `child.ts` with `AMOUNT=1300`, the smallest payment the executor sends. For a quick test, change `runs` to 1.
2. Give the parent wallet about 1,304 cNGN and a little CELO, then run `parent.ts` and answer `y`.
3. Remesso finds the schedule within about five minutes and sends the first payment. The child's terminal prints it, with the cash-out link, and marks it final about half an hour later.

## Where to go next

- [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests): listing, answering and declining requests.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/webhooks): the handler, the challenge and retries.
- [Give an AI agent a budget](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/ai-agent-budget): an agent that pays from a policy instead of signing schedules.
- The complete pair of agents: [examples/family-allowance-agent.ts](https://bitbucket.org/crackedstudios/remesso/src/main/examples/family-allowance-agent.ts).

# Give an AI agent a budget

> Cap what an agent's key can spend from a person's wallet, pay with idempotency keys so a retry never pays twice, and let the person review and revoke.

Source: https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/use-cases/ai-agent-budget

An AI agent that buys things for a person needs money it can spend, within limits the person trusts. Handing it a funded key trusts it with everything. With a policy, the person caps what the agent's key can pay: so much per payment, so much per day, for so many days, and optionally only to a fixed list of recipients. The agent pays from the person's wallet, and the contract refuses anything outside the policy.

## What you'll build

- `grant.ts`: the person creates the policy, once.
- `agent.ts`: the agent pays, with an idempotency key per payment and a store on disk, so a retry after a timeout or a crash never pays twice.
- Paying or declining a payment request sent to the person.
- `review.ts`: the person sees the policy, the agent's payments, and can revoke it.

## Prerequisites

- The setup from [Installation](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/installation).
- **The person:** a key holding the USDT the agent may spend, and a little CELO to sign the policy. With no CELO, the SDK pays that gas in USDT. The person can also set the policy up in the Remesso app at [remesso.xyz/agent-wallet](https://remesso.xyz/agent-wallet).
- **The agent:** its own key, generated for this and holding nothing of value. Agent payments are signed before they're sent, so they need a local account (`privateKeyToAccount`). The agent's key pays its own gas, so keep a little CELO in it. The SDK wants twice a payment's gas in hand before it signs, about 0.05 CELO at 200 gwei. Alternatively, a little USDT of its own then pays the gas.

Policy payments carry no fee: what the agent pays is what arrives. There's no per-payment minimum either: the executor's 1-dollar floor applies to schedules only.

## Step 1: The person grants a policy

```ts title="grant.ts"
import { createRemesso } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const person = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PERSON_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});

const policy = await person.policies.create({
  agent: process.env.AGENT_ADDRESS!, // the agent's key, which will call pay()
  token: "USDT",
  perPayment: "5", // at most 5 USDT a payment
  perDay: "20", // and 20 USDT in any rolling day
  days: 30, // it ends by itself after 30 days
  budget: "100", // added to your USDT approval for the allowance contract
  recipients: [process.env.SHOP!], // optional: the only addresses the agent may pay
});
console.log(`policy #${policy.id}: https://celoscan.io/tx/${policy.hash}`);
```

This sends two transactions: an approval, then the policy. `budget` is added to the person's USDT approval for the allowance contract. That approval is the most this policy and the person's other USDT policies can ever spend together, whatever the caps say. Leave out `recipients` to let the agent pay anyone. Whether a policy has a list is fixed when it's created. On a policy created with one, the person can add or remove recipients later with `policies.setRecipient(id, address, allowed)`.

## Step 2: The agent pays

Give every payment you intend its own idempotency key, such as an order or invoice id. The SDK signs the payment and records it in the store before broadcasting it. A retry with the same key then reports what became of that payment instead of making another.

```ts title="agent.ts"
import { createRemesso, RemessoError } from "remesso-sdk";
import { fileStore } from "remesso-sdk/node";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const agent = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.AGENT_KEY as `0x${string}`),
  store: fileStore(), // ~/.remesso-sdk/payments.json: a retry pays once, even after a restart
});

/// Pay for one order. Safe to call again with the same order id, after a timeout or a crash.
export async function payForOrder(orderId: string, shop: string, amount: string) {
  try {
    const r = await agent.pay({
      to: shop,
      amount, // decimal, in the policy's token: "2.50"
      token: "USDT",
      idempotencyKey: `order:${orderId}`, // one key per payment you intend
      memo: `order ${orderId}`, // up to 32 bytes, recorded on-chain
    });
    if (r.status === "pending") return { state: "pending", hash: r.hash } as const; // call again later, same order id
    return { state: r.repeat ? "already paid" : "paid", hash: r.hash, sent: r.sent } as const;
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof RemessoError && e.code === "refused") return { state: "refused", reason: e.message } as const;
    throw e;
  }
}
```

The agent can check its limits before it promises anything:

```ts
import { formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";

for (const id of await agent.policies.find()) {
  const p = await agent.policies.get(id);
  if (!p.active) continue;
  console.log(`policy #${p.id}: up to ${formatAmount(p.spendable, p.token)} now, ${formatAmount(p.remainingToday, p.token)} left today`);
}
```

`spendable` counts every limit at once: the per-payment cap, what's left of today, and the person's balance and approval.

### What `pay` answers

| What happened | What `pay` does | What the agent does |
|---|---|---|
| It landed | Returns `status: "confirmed"` | Done. |
| No receipt within 45 seconds (`waitMs`) | Returns `status: "pending"` | Call again later with the same key. |
| The same key again, after it paid | Returns `confirmed` with `repeat: true`, and sends nothing | Treat it as paid. |
| The same key for a different payment | Throws [`key_reused`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#key_reused) | Fix the bug: one key per payment. |
| An identical payment in the last ten minutes, without a key | Throws [`repeat`](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors#repeat) | Pass a key, or `allowRepeat` if you mean it. |
| Over a cap, revoked, expired, or a recipient not on the list | Throws `refused`, before anything is signed | Tell the person. |
| Mined, and reverted | Throws `reverted`: nothing moved | Use a new key to try again. |

A pending payment resolves on the next call with its key. If the transaction is in a block, the call reports the outcome. If it never left the machine, its own signed bytes go out now, with the same nonce, so it still pays at most once. If another transaction took its nonce and it never landed, it's paid afresh under the same key.

`fileStore` keeps a record for 30 days, up to 1,000 of them. Use one process per file: the file isn't locked. The default store is memory, which only protects retries inside one process.

## Step 3: Requests sent to the person

Other people and agents can ask the person to pay with a payment request. The agent sees the person's inbox and can answer a one-off request, such as an invoice, from the policy:

```ts
for (const r of await agent.requests.list(process.env.PERSON_WALLET)) {
  console.log(`${r.from ?? "someone"} asks for ${r.amount} ${r.token}: "${r.note ?? ""}" (${r.id})`);
}

// Pay it: its own amount, its reference as the memo, at most once per request.
await agent.requests.pay(requestId);

// Or turn it down, signed by the agent under the person's policy.
await agent.requests.decline(requestId, { policyId });
```

`requests.pay` pays only a request addressed to the policy's owner, from an active policy of the same token. Its idempotency key defaults to the request id, so paying the same request twice pays once. The memo carries the request's reference, so the requester sees it answered. A request for recurring payments asks for a schedule, which the person signs themselves.

## Step 4: The person reviews and revokes

```ts title="review.ts"
import { createRemesso, formatAmount } from "remesso-sdk";
import { privateKeyToAccount } from "viem/accounts";

const person = createRemesso({
  account: privateKeyToAccount(process.env.PERSON_KEY as `0x${string}`),
});
const policyId = BigInt(process.env.POLICY_ID!);

const p = await person.policies.get(policyId);
console.log(`policy #${p.id} for ${p.agent}: ${p.active ? "active" : p.revoked ? "revoked" : "expired"}`);
console.log(`${formatAmount(p.spendable, p.token)} spendable now, ${formatAmount(p.remainingToday, p.token)} left today`);

// Every payment made from this wallet under a policy, as Remesso's indexer reads it from the chain.
const { events } = await person.events.list({ role: "from", kinds: ["policy_payment"] });
for (const e of events.filter((x) => x.refId === p.id.toString())) {
  console.log(`${e.blockTime}  ${formatAmount(e.amount!, e.token!)} to ${e.to}  ${e.memoText ?? ""}`);
}

if (process.argv.includes("--revoke")) {
  console.log("revoked:", await person.policies.revoke(policyId)); // the agent's next payment is refused
}
```

Revoking takes effect at once, and no one can undo it, Remesso included. To give the agent a budget again, create a new policy.

## Test it safely

1. Grant a small policy: `perPayment: "0.05"`, `perDay: "0.10"`, `days: 1`, `budget: "0.10"`.
2. Send the agent's key a little CELO, then call `payForOrder("test-1", yourOtherWallet, "0.02")`.
3. Call it again with `"test-1"`: it answers `already paid`, and nothing new is sent.
4. Run `review.ts` to see the payment, then `review.ts --revoke`. A payment after that is refused.

## Where to go next

- [Agent payments](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/agent-payments): policies, stores and every option of `pay`.
- [Payment requests](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/guides/payment-requests): requests, references and declines.
- [Errors](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/reference/errors): every `RemessoError` code, and what to do about it.
- [Security](https://docs.remesso.xyz/docs/resources/security): what a policy protects, and what it doesn't.
